html:
SMTO-CFG-0035 — SMTO can't find the settings file it was told to use

GUID: 41c5811a-2a7c-498d-bf23-dc7356ebc3a7
Slug: config-explicit-app-config-not-found-at-check
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO was started with a specific settings file, but there is no file at that location, so it stopped. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find the file location in the error message and check that the file really exists there, including the spelling of the file and folder names. SMTO looks only at that exact location and doesn't search anywhere else.
  2. If the file was moved or renamed, start SMTO with its new location: run ./startup.sh --config followed by the file's full path. The --config option tells SMTO exactly which settings file to load.
  3. If SMTO is started by a script or service someone else set up, ask them to correct the AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH setting it uses. When that setting is present, SMTO uses its path instead of looking for config.yaml in its own folder.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message (it shows the location SMTO tried) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't create an empty file at that location just to get past this; SMTO would then start without the settings you meant to use.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration resolution failed because the path given by --config or AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH does not exist after expanding ~ and resolving it against the process working directory.

What this means

  • The explicitly selected --config or AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH resolves to a path that does not exist. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • The explicitly selected --config or AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH resolves to a path that does not exist.

How to diagnose it

  • Resolve the selected path relative to the process directory and check the explicit argument/environment precedence.

How to fix it

  • Compare the path printed in the message with the --config argument and the AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH environment variable (relative paths resolve from the process working directory, which is the SMTO folder for startup.sh). Correct or unset the explicit path; with neither set, SMTO loads config.yaml from the working directory if present, otherwise built-in defaults.
  • Correct --config or AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH to the intended existing file.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended explicit configuration file exists and loads through normal parsing.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
